detail.longDescription: Hi HN, I’m Sachin, and I’ve spent the last couple of months working on Faros Desktop, a Mac app that visualizes how you use your local AI coding tools into one place and then makes recommendations to make your subscription spend go further. As agents have replaced hands-on-keyboard work, the team and I wanted to better understand what’s in our session traces. Faros Desktop hydrates with on-device session history in Codex, Claude Code, Github Copilot, and Cursor to let users deep dive into a beautiful visualization of AI session traces. Then based on consolidating that information, the app shows patterns in usage as well as recommendations for ways to save spend through simple changes that we call Power Ups. Faros Desktop is totally free, with no login required and no API keys needed. The app also only uses on-device models to summarize local sessions in chunks, then organizes them by project and task. You can jump around a session timeline and see exactly the messages and tool calls in the trace. The business model here for Faros Desktop is to drive thought leadership and create leads for our sales team to sell the company’s multi-player Token Engineering Platform for large engineering organizations. Faros has been serving large engineering organizations for the past seven years, so it was cool to be able to build a product for all Builders, not just enterprise engineering orgs. One big direction we’re exploring: using previous sessions to make the next one better. We’re looking at local memory portability across harnesses as well as multi-player modes to share memory within your direct team. I’d love to hear thoughts on that.
